teachingAdditions: Storage units and decimal conversions

A bit is one binary digit; a nibble is 4 bits and a byte is 8 bits. Using decimal units: 1 KB = 1,000 bytes; 1 MB = 1,000 KB; 1 GB = 1,000 MB; 1 TB = 1,000 GB; 1 PB = 1,000 TB. For example, 2 MB = 2,000 KB = 2,000,000 bytes; 2 TB = 2,000 GB.
Character capacity and adjacent codes

With n bits there are 2^n distinct binary patterns: 7 bits permit 128 codes. A character set must provide enough distinct codes for its characters. Unicode has several encodings; do not assume every character uses one byte. Given A=65 and consecutive capital-letter codes, B=66 and C=67. Derive supplied neighbouring codes rather than memorising ASCII values.

options: Multitasking requires every application to run on a separate permanently dedicated CPU.

questions.answer: It can retain more frequently used data and instructions and reduce slower memory accesses.
questions.explanation: It can retain more frequently used data and instructions and reduce slower memory accesses.

questions.question: CPU A has 4 GHz, two cores and 2 MB cache. CPU B has 3 GHz, eight cores and 8 MB cache. Explain why neither can be declared fastest for every task.
questions.answer: A has more cycles per second, which may help a comparable single-threaded workload. B has more cores for parallel/concurrent work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Workload and architecture affect the result.
questions.explanation: A has more cycles per second, which may help a comparable single-threaded workload. B has more cores for parallel/concurrent work and more cache to reduce slow memory access. Workload and architecture affect the result.

questions.question: When is a count-controlled loop suitable?
questions.answer: When the number of repetitions is known or determined by a fixed count.
questions.explanation: When the number of repetitions is known or determined by a fixed count.

questions.question: A programmer plans an age-checking algorithm before implementing it. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: A structure diagram must show every runtime decision as a flowchart diamond.
It expresses ordered algorithmic steps without requiring the exact syntax of one programming language.
Pseudocode can only be written using valid machine-code instructions.
An algorithm's inputs are always the final calculated results.
questions.answer: B — It expresses ordered algorithmic steps without requiring the exact syntax of one programming language.
questions.explanation: It expresses ordered algorithmic steps without requiring the exact syntax of one programming language. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “A diamond is used only for unconditional calculations.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: A decision or condition with alternative paths.
questions.explanation: A decision or condition with alternative paths.

questions.question: A program calculates a bill and then applies a discount. A pupil claims: “Any order of instructions produces the same result.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: Unambiguous conditions and ordered steps allow the intended behaviour to be implemented and checked. The specified order and conditions must make the intended outcome follow for every permitted input.
questions.explanation: Unambiguous conditions and ordered steps allow the intended behaviour to be implemented and checked. The specified order and conditions must make the intended outcome follow for every permitted input.

questions.question: When is a condition-controlled loop suitable?
questions.answer: When repetition continues or ends according to a condition, such as valid input.
questions.explanation: When repetition continues or ends according to a condition, such as valid input.

questions.question: Linear-search [7, 2, 9, 4] for 4, starting at index 0. State the inspected values in order and number of comparisons.
options: Only inspect the first item, whatever the target.
Skip every item at an odd index.
[7, 2, 9, 4]; 4 comparison(s), found at index 3.
Stop without comparisons because linear search needs sorted data.
questions.answer: C — [7, 2, 9, 4]; 4 comparison(s), found at index 3.
questions.explanation: [7, 2, 9, 4]; 4 comparison(s), found at index 3. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “An IF statement must execute every possible branch regardless of its condition.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: It chooses a branch according to a condition; selection can be nested.
questions.explanation: It chooses a branch according to a condition; selection can be nested.

questions.question: (a) Perform one complete left-to-right ascending bubble-sort pass on [6, 1, 5, 3]. Give the array after each adjacent comparison and identify the value fixed at the right end.
questions.answer: (a) [[1, 6, 5, 3], [1, 5, 6, 3], [1, 5, 3, 6]]; largest value 6 is at the right end.
questions.explanation: (a) [[1, 6, 5, 3], [1, 5, 6, 3], [1, 5, 3, 6]]; largest value 6 is at the right end.

questions.question: Why must a trace table follow executed assignments in order?
questions.answer: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.
questions.explanation: Each variable value depends on the state produced by earlier executed instructions.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair of answers, in order. (1) Which data type is suitable for a count of pupils? (2) Which type can represent a measured distance of 2.75 km?
options: Fractional value required for every count / Fractional numeric value
Integer for a whole-number count / Whole numbers only
Fractional value required for every count / Whole numbers only
Integer for a whole-number count / Fractional numeric value
questions.answer: D — Integer for a whole-number count / Fractional numeric value
questions.explanation: (1) Integer, because the count is a whole number. (2) Real, because the value has a fractional part. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: How do character and string data differ?
questions.answer: A character represents one character; a string represents a sequence of characters.

prerequisite_notes: Explicitly distinguish a single character from a string.
questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: A program repeats the fixed limit 30 in five places. One copy is changed to 32 and the rest are missed. Explain how a named constant would help and how it differs from a changing score.
questions.answer: Define one appropriately named constant such as MAX_CLASS_SIZE and use its name at each point, so one deliberate definition change updates the limit consistently. A score is a variable because it changes during execution.
questions.explanation: Define one appropriately named constant such as MAX_CLASS_SIZE and use its name at each point, so one deliberate definition change updates the limit consistently. A score is a variable because it changes during execution.

questions.prerequisite_resolution: Included in New Learning of the cited source lesson

questions.question: What does sequence mean in programming?
questions.answer: Instructions execute in the specified order.
questions.explanation: Instructions execute in the specified order.

questions.question: A bill calculator multiplies a quantity by a unit price before adding a fee. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: 10, because multiplication is evaluated before addition.
Expressions always execute strictly left to right regardless of operator precedence.
Assignment permanently prevents a variable from changing again.
A constant is a variable whose value must change after every instruction.
questions.answer: A — 10, because multiplication is evaluated before addition.
questions.explanation: 10, because multiplication is evaluated before addition. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: What is 2 ^ 3 in OCR ERL?
questions.answer: 8; ^ denotes exponentiation in OCR ERL.
questions.explanation: 8; ^ denotes exponentiation in OCR ERL.
prerequisite_notes: Explicitly teach the exponentiation operator in OCR ERL.

questions.question: A program reads text '12'. Joining it to '3' gives one result, while converting it to an integer and adding 3 gives another. Give both results and explain what should happen for input 'twelve'.
questions.answer: Text concatenation gives 123. Integer conversion followed by numeric addition gives 15. Non-numeric text such as twelve cannot simply be assumed to cast successfully; handle or reject the invalid conversion.
questions.explanation: Text concatenation gives 123. Integer conversion followed by numeric addition gives 15. Non-numeric text such as twelve cannot simply be assumed to cast successfully; handle or reject the invalid conversion.

questions.question: A £5-per-ticket program uses total = tickets + 5. What is the correction?
questions.answer: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.
questions.explanation: Use total = tickets * 5; addition does not calculate £5 for each ticket.

questions.question: Insertion sort has sorted prefix [2, 5, 8] and next key 6. State which values must move, then give the new sorted prefix.
options: New prefix [2, 5, 8]; discard the key.
Values greater than 6 shift right: [8]. New prefix [2, 5, 6, 8].
New prefix [2, 5, 8, 6]; no comparison is needed.
New prefix [6, 2, 5, 8]; always place the key first.
questions.answer: B — Values greater than 6 shift right: [8]. New prefix [2, 5, 6, 8].
questions.explanation: Values greater than 6 shift right: [8]. New prefix [2, 5, 6, 8]. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “A comparison operator must always produce a text paragraph.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: A Boolean result indicating whether the comparison is true or false.
questions.explanation: A Boolean result indicating whether the comparison is true or false.

questions.question: A warning is raised if temperature is too high or pressure is too high. A pupil claims: “OR is false whenever both inputs are true.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: When at least one input is true, including when both are true. A case where just one condition is true distinguishes AND from OR; negation reverses the condition rather than testing both branches.
questions.explanation: When at least one input is true, including when both are true. A case where just one condition is true distinguishes AND from OR; negation reverses the condition rather than testing both branches.

questions.question: What does assignment do to a variable?
questions.answer: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.
questions.explanation: It stores a value in the named variable, replacing its previous value if one existed.

questions.question: A program must continue only while finished is false. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: Assignment permanently prevents a variable from changing again.
A constant is a variable whose value must change after every instruction.
It reverses true and false.
NOT always returns true regardless of its input.
questions.answer: C — It reverses true and false.
questions.explanation: It reverses true and false. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: What values does a Boolean variable represent?
questions.answer: True or false.
questions.explanation: True or false.
prerequisite_notes: Name Boolean as a data type as well as using Boolean conditions.

questions.question: Computers on a single school site share printers and files. Two school sites in different towns need to communicate. Two claims are made: (a) “A LAN must cover several countries.” (b) “A WAN can only connect computers within one room.” Correct each claim and justify the distinction.
questions.answer: (a) It connects devices across a relatively small geographical area, such as one school site. (b) It connects networks across a large geographical area, often using external communication infrastructure. The geographical scope and linked networks justify LAN or WAN; Internet access alone does not decide the category.
questions.explanation: (a) It connects devices across a relatively small geographical area, such as one school site. (b) It connects networks across a large geographical area, often using external communication infrastructure. The geographical scope and linked networks justify LAN or WAN; Internet access alone does not decide the category.

questions.question: What is the result of concatenating 'AB' and '12'?
questions.answer: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.
questions.explanation: AB12, with no automatically inserted space.

questions.question: A four-element array stores [4, 8, 2, 6]. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: The first index in every OCR ERL array is 1.
Concatenating two strings always adds their numeric values.
substring(1,3) always includes character positions 1 through 3 inclusive in every language.
A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.answer: D — A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.explanation: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “Testing a few inputs proves a program can never contain any fault.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.
questions.explanation: To identify faults and check behaviour against requirements using expected results.

questions.question: A programmer tests a new input routine before adding the payment routine. A completed booking program is checked before release. Two claims are made: (a) “Iterative testing happens only after the entire finished product is delivered.” (b) “Final testing removes any need for testing during development.” Correct each claim and justify the distinction.
questions.answer: (a) Testing and correcting parts during development as the solution is built. (b) Testing the completed solution against its requirements after development. Testing a component during development and checking the complete product at the end serve complementary purposes.
questions.explanation: (a) Testing and correcting parts during development as the solution is built. (b) Testing the completed solution against its requirements after development. Testing a component during development and checking the complete product at the end serve complementary purposes.

questions.question: What does input validation check?
questions.answer: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.
questions.explanation: Whether input meets specified rules; it does not prove factual truth or identity.
topics: Validation rules and rejection of invalid data

questions.question: Choose the correct pair of answers, in order. (1) For valid integer ages 13–18, give an invalid input of the correct type. (2) For a numeric age input, give erroneous data of the wrong type.
options: Correct type outside rules, e.g. 12 / Wrong type, e.g. text 'twelve'
Always wrong data type / Wrong type, e.g. text 'twelve'
Correct type outside rules, e.g. 12 / Always a valid in-range integer
Always wrong data type / Always a valid in-range integer
questions.answer: A — Correct type outside rules, e.g. 12 / Wrong type, e.g. text 'twelve'
questions.explanation: (1) 12 is an integer but outside the valid range, so it must be rejected. (2) The text 'twelve' is the wrong data type and must be handled or rejected. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “Defensive design assumes every user always enters valid and harmless data.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.
questions.explanation: Planning for invalid, unexpected or malicious use and handling it safely.

questions.question: A desktop needs a connection to a local network. A pupil claims: “A NIC's purpose is keeping files when power is off.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: The interface that enables a device to connect to a network. The correct device or medium must perform the required connection or forwarding role; the devices are not interchangeable.
questions.explanation: The interface that enables a device to connect to a network. The correct device or medium must perform the required connection or forwarding role; the devices are not interchangeable.

questions.question: What is a one-dimensional array?
questions.answer: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.
questions.explanation: A fixed-size indexed collection of related elements; OCR ERL indexing begins at zero.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair of answers, in order. (1) For valid ages 13–18, give an ordinary normal test value. (2) For valid ages 13–18, identify the two valid boundary values.
options: Wrong type required / Valid edge values 12 and 19
Ordinary valid input, e.g. 15 / Valid edge values 13 and 18
Wrong type required / Valid edge values 13 and 18
Ordinary valid input, e.g. 15 / Valid edge values 12 and 19
questions.answer: B — Ordinary valid input, e.g. 15 / Valid edge values 13 and 18
questions.explanation: (1) 15 is a representative valid value away from the boundaries. (2) 13 and 18 lie on the edges of the valid range. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “Any device connected to the Internet is automatically an embedded system.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: It is part of a larger heating system and performs the dedicated task of controlling temperature.
questions.explanation: It is part of a larger heating system and performs the dedicated task of controlling temperature.

questions.question: A pupil enters a website domain name rather than its IP address. A pupil claims: “DNS assigns the same MAC address to all computers visiting a website.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: Distributed DNS servers help look up the IP address associated with a domain name. The client requests a remote service; access depends on the relevant server and network services being available.
questions.explanation: Distributed DNS servers help look up the IP address associated with a domain name. The client requests a remote service; access depends on the relevant server and network services being available.

questions.question: How can a loop total an array's values?
questions.answer: Initialise a total and add each indexed value once while traversing the array.
questions.explanation: Initialise a total and add each indexed value once while traversing the array.

questions.question: A washing machine's controller monitors sensors and controls its wash cycle. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: Any device connected to the Internet is automatically an embedded system.
The CPU's main purpose is permanent file storage.
It is built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function, often with limited resources.
An embedded system must be a general-purpose desktop computer.
questions.answer: C — It is built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function, often with limited resources.
questions.explanation: It is built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function, often with limited resources. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “Adding active users always increases the bandwidth available to each user.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.
questions.explanation: Users may compete for finite bandwidth, reducing the data rate available to each.

questions.question: A school needs central accounts and controlled shared files. Three laptops share files directly for a small club. Two claims are made: (a) “In client-server networking every client must act as an identical dedicated server.” (b) “Peer-to-peer sharing always requires a dedicated central server.” Correct each claim and justify the distinction.
questions.answer: (a) It provides centrally managed services or resources requested by clients. (b) Devices can act as both clients and servers, sharing resources directly without requiring a dedicated central server. Central management suits school accounts, while direct sharing can be inexpensive for a small group but harder to administer at scale.
questions.explanation: (a) It provides centrally managed services or resources requested by clients. (b) Devices can act as both clients and servers, sharing resources directly without requiring a dedicated central server. Central management suits school accounts, while direct sharing can be inexpensive for a small group but harder to administer at scale.

questions.question: How is a cell selected in a two-dimensional array?
questions.answer: Using two indices, such as a row index and a column index.
questions.explanation: Using two indices, such as a row index and a column index.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair of answers, in order. (1) What is a router's main network role? (2) What does a switch do within a LAN?
options: Calculates spreadsheet formulas / Forwards within LAN using MAC
Routes between networks using IP / Broadcasts every unicast frame to all ports
Calculates spreadsheet formulas / Broadcasts every unicast frame to all ports
Routes between networks using IP / Forwards within LAN using MAC
questions.answer: D — Routes between networks using IP / Forwards within LAN using MAC
questions.explanation: (1) It forwards traffic between different networks using IP addressing. (2) It forwards data towards the appropriate connected device using MAC-address information. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “An IPv4 address is always six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: It supports network addressing and routing; commonly four decimal numbers separated by dots.
questions.explanation: It supports network addressing and routing; commonly four decimal numbers separated by dots.

questions.question: Tablets need wireless access to a school's wired LAN. A pupil claims: “A WAP's main job is converting domain names into IP addresses.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: It enables wireless devices to connect to the network. The correct device or medium must perform the required connection or forwarding role; the devices are not interchangeable.
questions.explanation: It enables wireless devices to connect to the network. The correct device or medium must perform the required connection or forwarding role; the devices are not interchangeable.

questions.question: What is a record?
questions.answer: A structured collection of named fields describing one entity, potentially using different data types.
questions.explanation: A structured collection of named fields describing one entity, potentially using different data types.

questions.question: A programmer changes an upper-bound comparison from < to <=. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: To check that the fault is fixed and that other required behaviour still works.
Correcting one line proves the entire program is now fault-free without further testing.
Testing a few inputs proves a program can never contain any fault.
Iterative testing happens only after the entire finished product is delivered.
questions.answer: A — To check that the fault is fixed and that other required behaviour still works.
questions.explanation: To check that the fault is fixed and that other required behaviour still works. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “The Internet is a single computer containing every website.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: A worldwide collection of interconnected computer networks.
questions.explanation: A worldwide collection of interconnected computer networks.

questions.question: A school wants its website available when a visitor's browser requests a page. A pupil claims: “A web client must host every website before it can request a page.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: A server stores and makes website resources available for clients to request. The client requests a remote service; access depends on the relevant server and network services being available.
questions.explanation: A server stores and makes website resources available for clients to request. The client requests a remote service; access depends on the relevant server and network services being available.

questions.question: What distinguishes a function from a procedure?
questions.answer: A function returns a value to its caller; a procedure performs a task without returning a function value.
questions.explanation: A function returns a value to its caller; a procedure performs a task without returning a function value.

questions.question: A user presses Send on a new email. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: Bluetooth is normally the best choice for a high-capacity link between distant school sites.
Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.
SMTP's role is synchronising folders and read status across mail clients.
Wi-Fi requires a separate physical cable from every mobile device to the switch.
questions.answer: B — Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.
questions.explanation: Sending email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “Cloud storage guarantees that files remain accessible during every Internet outage.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: Remote resources such as storage, software or processing accessed over a network; availability and connectivity matter.
questions.explanation: Remote resources such as storage, software or processing accessed over a network; availability and connectivity matter.

questions.question: A school buys compatible networking equipment from different manufacturers. A pupil claims: “Standards require all network devices to come from the same manufacturer.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: Agreed specifications help hardware and software from different producers interoperate. Compatible interfaces let the products exchange data without requiring a single manufacturer.
questions.explanation: Agreed specifications help hardware and software from different producers interoperate. Compatible interfaces let the products exchange data without requiring a single manufacturer.

teachingAdditions: Local and global constants as well as variables

A local variable or constant is accessible within its defining local scope. A global variable or constant has wider program scope. Constants are intended to stay fixed during execution; variables may change. Unnecessary mutable global state makes unintended changes harder to track.

questions.question: When might a procedure be suitable?
questions.answer: For a named reusable task such as displaying a menu when no function result is required.
questions.explanation: For a named reusable task such as displaying a menu when no function result is required.

questions.question: In OCR ERL, s = 'VARIABLE'. Give s.substring(1,3), then explain what each argument means.
options: AR; second argument is an exclusive end index.
IAB; start at index 3.
ARI; start at zero-based index 1 and take 3 characters.
VAR; indexing starts at 1.
questions.answer: C — ARI; start at zero-based index 1 and take 3 characters.
questions.explanation: ARI; start at zero-based index 1 and take 3 characters. The other options describe a different operation or contain the stated misconception.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “Failure of any one workstation cable necessarily disables all other star-network links.” State the correction and explain it briefly.
questions.answer: Devices depending on that switch lose communication through it; a single workstation cable failure is usually localised.
questions.explanation: Devices depending on that switch lose communication through it; a single workstation cable failure is usually localised.

questions.question: A network must continue operating if one connection fails. A pupil claims: “A mesh has exactly one possible path between every pair of devices.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.
questions.answer: Alternative paths can allow communication after some links fail, at the cost of more links and complexity. Resilience comes from the topology’s available paths; costs and central points of failure must still be considered.
questions.explanation: Alternative paths can allow communication after some links fail, at the cost of more links and complexity. Resilience comes from the topology’s available paths; costs and central points of failure must still be considered.

teachingAdditions: Passing and returning an array

A function may receive an array as an argument, process it and return an array result. For example, receive [2,4,6], create a new array by adding 1 to each element, then return [3,5,7]. The caller must use the returned result. Passing the input and returning the output are separate actions; the original changes only if the implementation changes it.

questions.question: What is a parameter?
questions.answer: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.
questions.explanation: A named input received by a subprogram when called with an argument.

questions.question: An urgent fake school message asks a pupil to enter their password through a link. Which statement correctly explains this situation?
options: Phishing is the process of trying every possible password automatically.
Malware means any program that uses a large amount of RAM.
Brute force works only by physically breaking the computer.

questions.question: A pupil writes: “Fibre carries electrical signals through copper wire.” State the correction and explain it briefly.

questions.question: A wireless keyboard is used close to a computer. Which statement correctly explains this situation?

questions.question: A LAN switch needs to forward data to interface 02:11:22:33:44:55. Which statement correctly explains this situation?

questions.explanation: It applies rules to allow or block network traffic.

questions.question: Data must reach the correct remote destination in the correct order. A pupil claims: “TCP's purpose is choosing fonts and IP's purpose is drawing images.” Correct the claim and explain one consequence in this situation.

Concatenating two strings always adds their numeric values.
substring(1,3) always includes character positions 1 through 3 inclusive in every language.
A structured collection of named fields describing one entity, potentially using different data types.

questions.answer: Data or an instruction being transferred to or from memory.
questions.explanation: Data or an instruction being transferred to or from memory.

grid[1,0] is 12; 12 is at grid[1,0].

questions.question: A microphone signal is recorded as a digital audio file. A pupil claims: “Sampling stores every possible instant of a continuous sound wave.” Correct the claim and explain its consequence here.
questions.answer: Measure amplitude at regular intervals and store quantised sample values in binary. Discrete measurements approximate the continuous signal; the choices of rate and bit depth limit captured detail.
